description: Reads a bank statement file and writes its statements and lines. `format` says what the file is — `camt.053` (the ISO 20022 XML statement), `coda`, `cfonb120`, or `csv` with the account it is of (`bank_account_id`) and the profile of its columns (`csv_profile`, kept on the account once an import with it succeeds, and read from there when left out), which are the ones this server reads today — and `content` is the file as text. It is never guessed from the content. It books nothing: every line waits as pending, to be settled afterwards. Safe to repeat: the same file imported twice creates nothing the second time, and a statement overlapping an earlier one imports only the new lines. Refused by name, with nothing written: an account the company does not have (create it first with create_bank_account — an import never creates one), a statement whose opening balance plus lines is not its closing balance, a line in another currency. Signalled in `warnings`, not refused: an opening balance that is not the previous closing one, which means a statement is missing.

bank_account_id.description: Only for a file of one statement whose account the company identifies otherwise than the file does. Left out, the account is found by the identifier the statement carries, and an unknown one is refused.

closing_balance.description: Only for `csv`: the closing balance the bank shows, the same way.

company_id.description: The company to work in. Ask list_companies if unsure.

csv_profile.description: Only for `csv`: the lay-out of the file. Left out, the profile kept on the bank account (`statement_profile` in list_bank_accounts) is used, and the import is refused csv_profile_required only when the account has none. Given, and the import succeeds, it is kept on the account for every later file of that bank, whoever imports it. A CSV names no account either, so `bank_account_id` is required with it.

columns.description: Which column says what, by header or by position from 1. `date` is required, and either `amount` or `debit`/`credit`. A `fee` column makes a second line of each row with a fee. A `balance` column (the running balance) proves the statement.

dateFormat.description: How a date is written, with DD, MM and YYYY (or YY): `DD/MM/YYYY`, `MM/DD/YYYY`, `YYYY-MM-DD`.

delimiter.description: The character between two fields: `,`, `;`, a tab, `|`.

header.description: Whether the first row read is a header. Default true; without one, columns are named by position.

newestFirst.description: The file lists the newest row first.

sign.description: `inverted` when a positive amount is money out, as a card statement writes a purchase.

skipFooterRows.description: Rows at the end that are not movements: a total.

skipRows.description: Lines above the header: a title, an account line.

thousandsSeparator.description: The mark between groups of three digits, when the file writes one.

file_name.description: The name the file had, kept on the statement.

format.description: What the file is. Required, and never guessed from the content: `camt.053` is the ISO 20022 XML statement, `coda` the coded statement of account of 128-character records, `cfonb120` the statement of 120-character records, `csv` a statement exported as CSV, read with `csv_profile`.

iban_country.description: Only for `cfonb120`, which identifies an account by a bank code, a branch code and a number, and names no country. With the two letters of the country the account is held in, the statement is matched on the IBAN those make there; left out, on the three joined, as written. Never guessed.

opening_balance.description: Only for `csv` without a running balance column: the opening balance the bank shows for the period, as a decimal string. The import needs both balances to prove no line is missing.

storage_path.description: Where the caller stored the file, if it did. With it the file is recorded in attachments, on the statement; this server stores no bytes.

name: import_bank_statement
title: Import a bank statement
